newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber prices end up in featureless trade.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber prices end up in featureless trade.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed higher in featureless trading as market participants were either on holiday or have closed their books for the year, dealers said.
They said prices continued to be supported by tight supply of raw materials due to seasonal rains which have reduced tapping activities at plantations.
"It's super quiet. We did not do anything today," said one local dealer. "The same can be expected tomorrow."
He said he expected some fresh inquiries after the New Year holiday.

At the close, January RSS1 buyer was quoted at 316 cents ($1.25) a kg by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board, up a cent from Friday. January SMR 20 buyer was up half cent at 310 cents ($1.23) a kg.
Dealers maintained their offer prices, quoting SMR CV at 367 cents, SMR L at 349, SMR 5 at 322, SMR 10 at 310, SMR 20 at 309 and drum latex at 241.
The INRO five-day moving average was 241.53 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Dec 27 against 241.86 on Dec 26. The daily indicator price was 241.52 versus 241.57.
